_what: SSOT for the 4 Claude Max accounts: identity map (launcher -> config dir -> email -> mailbox -> Dia profile) + router/endpoint config. Consumed by bin/claude-accounts, /accounts, scripts/handoff-fire.sh, skills/account-relogin. Deployed as a symlink at ~/.claude/accounts.json (install.sh); the knowledge-layer mirror shares it into every account config dir.
_secrets: NO tokens live here, ever. OAuth tokens stay in the macOS Keychain (item 'Claude Code-credentials-<sha256(config-dir)[:8]>', account = keychain_account). Emails are fine: this repo is private.
_order: accounts[] order = operator spend priority (next > next4 > next3 > next2, resume-sessions REFERENCE.md operator policy 2026-07-04).
_fable: There is no per-account Fable LAUNCHER any more (launcher consolidation, 2026-08-01): `claude-fable*` was only ever the row's launcher with a model env var, so the frontier tier is a MODEL, not a second entrypoint. Two routes, both live: pick `Fable` in the in-session /model picker (operator-confirmed 2026-08-01 on 2.1.220 — it is row 3, so this is the normal way in), or start pinned with `<launcher> --model claude-fable-5` when a session must BE Fable from turn one (fired peers, headless runs). The `fable_launcher` key is GONE because its value named a deleted command; `fable_name` STAYS (a bare CLI shorthand, not a launcher name) and gen-account-map.sh builds the fable pattern from it alone.
_port_index: port_index is a SEPARATE, frozen numbering used only for cc-authbrowser's per-account CDP port (PORT_BASE + port_index) — deliberately independent of accounts[] array order (contract SS1) so reordering accounts[] for spend priority never reshuffles a live CDP port. Optional per account; an entry with no port_index gets the next unused integer, so appending accounts never renumbers existing ones. fable_name/aliases are also optional (bare CLI shorthand for the fable variant, and extra config-dir basenames that resolve to this account).
_claude_bin: FALLBACK ONLY — not the answer. The eval binary is DERIVED by bin/cc-claude-bin from the `claude()` launcher's own `_bin=` line in ~/.zshrc, because that line is what actually starts every interactive session. This key is read only when the resolver is absent (a stripped $HOME, a hermetic fixture). WHY IT IS NOT THE SSOT: as a literal it pinned ~/.claude-219 while the launcher ran ~/.claude-220 (measured 2026-08-09), so probe_account()'s certification and cc-relogin's two login legs were all describing a build no session runs — the same drift scripts/handoff-fire.sh:225-228 records from the ~/.claude-183-vs-219 week. A copy of a version number cannot detect that the original moved; expect this value to rot, and do not trust it over the resolver. tests/account-fact-derivation.bats asserts the derived value agrees across claude-accounts, handoff-fire.sh and cc-claude-bin.
_spend: The pay-as-you-go guard, and the ONLY thing standing between pool exhaustion and a bill. usage_credits_authorized is the operator's standing answer to "may this fleet spend beyond the four Max subscriptions" — false means extra-usage credits are NOT sanctioned, so any nonzero extra_usage.used_credits on any account is a BREACH to surface, not a stat to render. It lives here because it lived nowhere: the guard existed only as a backlog row, with no field, no assertion and no test, which is the advisory-behind-a-diode failure — a standing cost guard that can only be remembered is one that will be forgotten while the meter runs. Note the unit trap the endpoint sets: extra_usage.used_credits is in CENTS (a reading of 17691 rendered as $176.91 in the web Usage panel), and credits_on is the TOGGLE, NOT a proxy for whether money moved — the same account read credits_on=false with $176.91 already spent. So the breach keys on SPEND, never on the toggle.

spend.breach_note: flip to true only on an explicit operator decision, and say why in the commit

_lock: lock_wait_s = how long a caller waits for the single-flight lock before serving a grace-TTL cache instead of blocking (the holder can own it for minutes: 4 accounts x keychain + 90s heal + retry ladders). cache_grace_s = the widened TTL used ONLY on that degrade path. --fresh NEVER degrades — handoff-fire relies on it forcing a live sweep with auto-heal.
_login: login_warn_h = how far ahead the LOGIN cliff is surfaced. The cliff is the keychain payload's refreshTokenExpiresAt: once it passes, every refresh grant returns invalid_grant and only an interactive /login recovers the account. It is anchored to the last INTERACTIVE login and is NOT extended by a refresh — observed 2026-07-24: next and next2 were both refreshed within the same minute yet carried refresh-token expiries 15 days apart. So it is a hard, unavoidable, perfectly-predictable, roughly-monthly-per-account cliff, and lead time is the only defence. 72h ~= three sweeps of warning; Claude Code's own startup banner does not warn until 24h.
_relogin: relogin_trigger_h = the RENEWAL-ATTEMPT window, and a different question from login_warn_h. login_warn_h asks 'how much lead time does a HUMAN need' (72h ~= three sweeps). This asks 'how many chances does the unattended executor get', and the answer is governed by a constraint the human surface does not have: cc-relogin can only act when the account has ZERO live sessions, so the window's job is to convert one fragile attempt into ~168 hourly chances to catch a k==0 moment on a busy account (docs/runbooks/RELOGIN_ACTIVATION.md section 5: 'renew at T-7d, not the 72h warn'). It is ONE constant because it is consumed by three programs that must agree: claude-accounts --relogin-status renders DUE inside it, cc-relogin-poll asks --login-status --window-h for exactly it, and cc-relogin's own gate accepts inside it. They drifted once (2026-07-29): the board rendered DUE and printed 'NEXT ACTION: cc-relogin next' across 72-168h while cc-relogin still gated on login_warn_h and exited 2 REFUSED — a 96-hour dead band in which the prescribed command could not run. tests/cc-relogin-status.bats re-proves the agreement by EXECUTING the board's own next_action.

frontier._: Window end/active are READ LIVE from model_config_ssot frontier_access (never hardcode a date — the reso-quota JUL7 lesson). coupling = fable_cap/weekly_cap per SSOT '<=50% of weekly usage limits'. end_date_inclusive: SSOT 'end:' means available THROUGH that date. credits_authorized: keep scoring Fable past the window deadline (deprioritized by CF) instead of hard-excluding — flip only on explicit operator authorization.

router._: Verified scoring constants (design->judge->5 adversarial verifiers, 2026-07-04; see resume-sessions REFERENCE.md section 6). KMAX raised 4 -> 8 on 2026-07-10: the old counter only saw --resume sessions (k<=1); the fixed counter sees ALL live sessions (observed 5-6 on primary accounts as deliberate operator practice), so KMAX=4 would have hard-excluded the priority accounts. M7 additions 2026-08-10 (ACCOUNT_ROUTING_V2 M7, all OPTIONAL — code defaults match): URGENCY_EXP = deadline exponent (score = headroom/T^g; 1 restores linear — the live 2026-08-10 snapshot scored {19% left, resets 27.8h} BELOW {87% left, resets 122h} under linear, starving the expiring account); KWORK_WINDOW_MIN = transcript-mtime minutes that count a session as WORKING (k_work replaces the pane census in KMAX/KF — census read k=28 on an account whose 5h window sat at 60%, i.e. panes are not burn); ASSIGN_TTL_MIN = minutes a fire-time --assign counts as a phantom working session (burst fires spread inside the 90s cache TTL instead of stacking on rank[0]); PROJ_LOOKAHEAD_H = hours SF projects 5h burn ahead (capped at the 5h reset; soften-only).
router._desk: W1 additions 2026-08-11 (DESK_ROUTER_AND_STARTUP_V1 W1 / docs/research/R2, all OPTIONAL — code defaults match, and range-checked by _validate_router when present). The desk lane (--route interactive, i.e. bare `claude`) is a two-key SORT, not a product of factors: 5h-safe set first, then EARLIEST WEEKLY RESET. DESK_5H_FLOOR = projected 5h utilisation below which an account is 5h-safe; 0.60 is sized by ARGUMENT, not by measurement (below S_CUT=0.85 with margin, above the 61% ceiling three accounts observed in 38h) — the replay was flat for every floor tried because the fleet almost never approaches 60%, so this is absence of evidence, NOT validation. DESK_W_FLOOR = weekly headroom at/above which an account is weekly-safe; it made no difference on this data (0/324) and exists only to stop a pure earliest-reset sort routing the desk to an account with 2% of its week left. Both keys DEGRADE one at a time (safe-set -> 5h-safe -> all eligible) and can never empty the candidate set. DESK_HYST_MARGIN = fraction a rival must beat the incumbent desk account by (churn measured 43.4% over the last 100 decisions; per-account projects/sessions make a flip cost --resume). DESK_HYST_TTL_MIN = minutes a `--assign --src claude-launcher` row still names the incumbent (300 = one 5h window). Kills: CC_ROUTE_DESK_5H_FLOOR=off, CC_ROUTE_DESK_W_FLOOR=off, CC_ROUTE_DESK_HYST=off, CC_ROUTE_DESK_ASSIGN_EXEMPT=off.
